title: Measure next-token cross entropy
statement:
Step 4 · Probabilities and loss

For each position, cross entropy is the negative log probability of the correct next token. Use log-sum-exp directly so an extremely small probability does not become log(0).

Build it

Return the mean cross entropy in natural-log units over aligned, nonempty logits and valid target IDs. Every row has a common vocabulary size.

Contract: Implement loss using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: logits = [[0, 0], [2, 0]], targets = [0, 0]
Expected: 0.410037595801459
Input: logits = [[1000, 1001, 999]], targets = [1]
Expected: 0.40760596444442854
Hint

For one row use max(row) + log(sum(exp(score−max))) − score[target].

Review your understanding

What does a loss of log(vocabulary size) tell you about a uniform model?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
